At the usual fortnighly meeting of this Society, held in St. John's Schoolroom on Tuesday evening, the president, the Rev. J. D. Milne, gave a series of read- raga from well-known authors. The principal reading which was much appreciated by those present was from" The Bonnie Brier Bush," by Dr. J. Watson (" lan MacLaren ") and gave a vivid picture of simple Scottish country life in a Highland parish. The read- ings and authors were discussed by several of the members, and Mr. Milne was accorded a hearty vote of thanks. ASK for CUNNINGHAM'S HIGFI-CLASS MINERAL WATERS.—Advt. PUBLIC BENEFIT. UNDER THE CLOCK FOR BEST BOOTS IN LANCASHIRE.—Advt. . irafaigar Day.---Alderman Bennett's Offer. Today (Saturday) is the centenary of Trafalgar Day. At the meeting of the Education Committee csa Monday it was decided to ask the teachers in the day schools to make suitable reference to the occasion on Friday. The Chairman tAlderman Bennett) said he proposed to ask the committee to accept a shield con- • taining copper from the Victory and, subject to their approval, to offer an annual prize for the best essay on" An Englishman's idea of duty" or some similar flbject, the prizes to be open to the upper standards sn all the schools and to be awarded annually upon Trafalgar Day, the shield to be held by the school in which the successful competitor is a pupil. (Hear, hear). PUBLIC BKNEFIT.—UNDER THE CLOCK FOR BEST BOOTS IN LANCASHIRE.—Advt. Memorial Window Unveiled. A special service was held at St. James' Church on Wednesday evening when a window to the memory of the late Rev. Francis Slater, for 20 years vicar of • the parishovas unveiled. The service was conducted by the Rev. D. R. Davies, the lessons being read by the Vicar (the Rev. H. B. Firth) and the Rev. Canon Morley Stevenson. At the conclusion of the service • there was a processional hymn a halt being made in front of the window which was unveiled by Mr. C. S. Burgess. The dedication prayer was recited by the Vicar. Returning to the chancel a sermon was Preached by the Rev. W. Stanton who chose as his subject the dedication of the window,and who fittingly referred to the long services to the parish by the late Rev. Francis Slater. The window is a companion window to one erected to. the memory of Mrs. Slater, and depicts our Lord giving the pastoral charge to St. Peter in the words " Feed my sheep." H. M. The " Realms of the Mikado" will be illustrated next week at the Parr Hall by "over 8,000 square feet of beautifully painted Tableaux" we are assured .by the proprietors that the Colossal views are abso- lutely authentic and are promised the depiction of the industries, amusements, cities, temples, tea gardens, theatres, and conan.erce of Japan which should at this time be exceptionally interesting. Not only pictures but living representatives of the far east will be pre- sented including the "Geisha" Yet-Ta a young lady of 'exceptional dexterity on the wire who executes a coon dance (or her idea of iDiduring her graceful perform- ance. There will also boa" Japanese Magician." A full English concert party and" something extra "in the way of animated photographs. The whole Promises well for an excellent and unique evenings' amusement. It is a far call to visit Japan but just now the more one knows of the plucky little Jap and his picturesque nation the better, and this opportunity of extending ones acquaintance with :things Japanese hould not be missed. Bond. Warrington lost one of the most popular of its Younger townsmen on Wednesday, when Mr. Cecil H. Bond of Latchford left for British Columbia by the " Oceanic." Mr. Bond is a native of Farnworth, but ',las for several years resided in theWarrington district and worked for Messrs Wright, Garnett and Wright, architects. Daring that time he has formed a large .•tcle of friends, and rendered excellent service to the arrington Dramatic Society and the Stockton Heath _l(,_ockey Club. His intention is to join a friend now at l'elowna, British Columbia, and enter into fruit-farm- ing- Mr. Bond left Warrington by the 1-50 train from -the Central Station on Wednesday and received a hearty send-off from friends and relatives both here and on the Liverpool landing stage.— Saturday evening a hot-pot supper and ;410king concert were given in Mr. Bond's !i.?nour by the Stockton Heath Hockey Club at the tlon Hotel. There was a splendid muster of mem- Prs of the club and other friends of Mr. Bond, fully 'ighty being present. Mr. E. Pierpoint presided, and tel the excellent supper provided by Mr. Lee, speech- :kin songs, and presentations followed one another .el rapid succession. The health of the guest of the veTting was enthusiastically drank, and he was the ‘r,e,cipient also of a repeating ride from the Hockey a revolver from Messrs. Wright, Garnett, and _vvorrt and employees, and a case of pipes from Farn- -7 h friends. The proceedings were of a most con- nature, and terminated with hearty individual and 4 collective wishes for Mr. Bond's " success " and '4 G ood luck."
